nodes.name: Binary search on a sorted array
nodes.description: Compare with the middle element and discard the half that cannot hold the target; O(log n).

facets.recognize: Spots sorted or monotonic input where a lookup must beat O(n).
facets.explain: States the invariant (if the target exists it is inside [low, high]) and why each step can drop half.
facets.implement: Writes low/high/mid with mid = low + (high - low) / 2, the right loop condition and updates that always shrink the range.
facets.trace: Gives low, high and mid for every iteration on a small input.

misconceptions.desc: Computed mid as (low + high) / 2, which overflows int when low + high exceeds INT_MAX.
Set low = mid or high = mid with a loop condition that never shrinks the range (loops forever on two elements).
Used low < high where low <= high was needed (or the reverse), skipping the last candidate or reading past the range.
Scanned linearly or nested loops on sorted input where binary search applies.
Applied binary search to data that is neither sorted nor monotonic.

nodes.name: Lower / upper bound and first / last occurrence
nodes.description: On a match, record it and keep searching toward the boundary: first index >= x, first index > x, floor, ceil.

facets.recognize: Maps first/last position, insert position, floor/ceil and count of x onto lower and upper bound.
facets.explain: Explains why the search continues after a match and why count = upper bound - lower bound.
facets.implement: Keeps an answer variable with the right default (n or -1) and moves the correct side on equality.
facets.adapt: Derives floor, ceil, insert position and occurrence count from the two bounds; uses std::lower_bound / upper_bound correctly.

misconceptions.desc: Returned on the first match instead of continuing toward the boundary; first/last occurrence is wrong with duplicates.
Moved the wrong side on equality (lower bound must go left when arr[mid] >= x; upper bound only when arr[mid] > x).
Defaulted the answer to -1 or 0 where 'past the end' must be n (insert position, lower bound).
Found one match, then walked left/right linearly; O(n) when every element equals the target.
Mixed up floor (largest <= x) and ceil (smallest >= x).

nodes.name: Binary search on a rotated sorted array
nodes.description: In a rotated sorted array at least one half around mid is sorted; decide which, then check whether the target lies inside it.

facets.recognize: Recognizes rotated sorted input (search, minimum, rotation count) as still binary-searchable.
facets.explain: Explains why one half is always sorted and how that decides which half to drop.
facets.implement: Identifies the sorted half with arr[low] <= arr[mid] and tests the target against that half's inclusive range.
facets.adapt: Handles duplicates (shrink both ends when arr[low] == arr[mid] == arr[high]); finds the minimum and the rotation count.

misconceptions.desc: Used the wrong test to find the sorted half, so the search dropped the half holding the target.
Used strict comparisons when checking whether the target lies inside the sorted half, missing targets at its ends.
With duplicates, did not handle arr[low] == arr[mid] == arr[high], where the sorted half cannot be told apart.
While finding the minimum, discarded a sorted half without first recording its smallest element.
Found the rotation point with a linear scan.

nodes.name: Binary search on the answer
nodes.description: When feasibility is monotonic in the answer (if x works, so does x + 1), binary search the smallest or largest feasible x, checking each with a greedy pass.

facets.recognize: Spots minimize-the-maximum / maximize-the-minimum and 'smallest value that still works' wording.
facets.explain: Explains why feasibility is monotonic and why the answer range runs from its smallest to largest possible value.
facets.implement: Sets the answer range correctly (e.g. max element .. sum), writes a correct greedy feasibility check and records the best feasible mid.
facets.adapt: Switches direction for max-of-min vs min-of-max, and searches over doubles with a precision bound.

misconceptions.desc: Tried every candidate answer linearly without noticing that feasibility is monotonic.
Chose a search range that excludes the answer or admits impossible ones (low = 1 instead of the largest element, high too small).
The feasibility check overflowed int (summed hours or days, or mid raised to a power).
Moved toward the wrong side after a feasible check (minimizing keeps going left; maximizing keeps going right).
The feasibility check is wrong: forgot to count the first group, or allowed one element larger than the limit.
Searched over doubles with an exact-equality stop or too few iterations, so the answer missed the required precision.

nodes.name: Binary search on a partition
nodes.description: Binary search how many elements to take from the smaller array so both left parts together form the first half (median, kth element).

facets.explain: Explains the cut condition l1 <= r2 and l2 <= r1, and why searching the smaller array keeps the other cut in range.
facets.implement: Uses INT_MIN / INT_MAX for empty sides and computes the median for odd and even total length.
facets.adapt: Turns the median search into a kth-element search by clamping the range to [max(0, k - n2), min(k, n1)].

misconceptions.desc: Binary searched over the larger array, so the other array's cut went negative or past its end.
Read l1, l2, r1 or r2 out of bounds instead of using INT_MIN / INT_MAX when a side is empty.
Got the median wrong for odd total length (left part must hold (n1 + n2 + 1) / 2 elements).
Merged both arrays in O(n + m) when O(log min(n, m)) was required.
For the kth element, did not clamp the search range to [max(0, k - n2), min(k, n1)].

nodes.name: Binary search on a local property
nodes.description: Discard half the range using a local fact (the slope at mid, pair parity) even when the array is not globally sorted.

facets.recognize: Sees that peak-finding and the single-element-in-pairs problem can drop half using a local comparison.
facets.explain: Explains why moving toward the higher neighbour always reaches a peak, or why pair parity reveals the side of the single element.
facets.implement: Compares with neighbours safely at the array ends.

misconceptions.desc: Compared arr[mid] with arr[mid - 1] or arr[mid + 1] without guarding mid at the ends.
Got the pair rule wrong (before the single element, pairs start at even indices).
Believed binary search needs sorted data, so scanned linearly.

nodes.name: Binary search in a matrix
nodes.description: Treat a fully sorted matrix as one array (row = i / cols, col = i % cols); walk from the top-right corner in a row- and column-sorted matrix; binary search columns for a 2D peak or values for a median.

facets.recognize: Picks the right search for how the matrix is sorted: whole matrix, rows and columns, or rows only.
facets.implement: Maps a flat index with the column count, and starts the staircase walk at a corner where one move increases and the other decreases.
facets.adapt: Finds a median by binary searching the value and counting elements <= mid in each row with upper bound.

misconceptions.desc: Mapped the flat index with the row count instead of the column count.
Started the staircase walk at the top-left or bottom-right, where both moves change the value the same way.
Binary searched every row (O(n log m)) when the whole matrix is sorted and one search over n * m cells suffices.
Found the matrix median by flattening and sorting instead of binary searching the value and counting.
